Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helix AI tranche simulation & recommended reserve sizes

Team —

Quick ask from the Helix deal team (deal HLX-2028-Q3-47): they want a recommended tranche/reserve plan across US / EU / APAC for a two-wave onramp. Can you run a short Monte Carlo-style simulation using the traffic profiles attached and produce: 
- a recommended committed tranche size per region (low / median / high scenarios)
- suggested commit triggers (usage thresholds, time windows)
- an ops-safe buffer for burst windows (SLO: 99th latency target 250ms for their primary model)

Attached: tranche_sim_input.csv (baseline QPS + seq length distribution). Please treat Helix as priority — lead time for the decision is EOD Friday.

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Sales, EMEA & APAC
Redwood Inference

(attachment: tranche_sim_input.csv)

Subject: Re: Helix AI tranche simulation & recommended reserve sizes

Naomi —

On it. Quick clarifying q's before I run the full sim:
1) Do we treat EU traffic as GDPR-restricted (no cross-region KV cache sharing)?
2) Are we modeling burst windows as 3x baseline for sustained 10 minute periods or as short spikes (30s)?
3) Which model variant should we optimize for? (Helix sent two: xl-general and xl-lowmem)

I'll take the baseline input and iterate — I'll attach an initial sim CSV with param sweeps once the first run completes.

Ben

Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helix AI tranche simulation & recommended reserve sizes

Ben / Naomi —

Attached are the first-pass sim outputs and a visualization of tail-risk across regions. High-level conclusions: 
- US: median recommended committed tranche = 56 GPUs; 90p = 72, 10p = 38. Burst buffer: +15% for 30s spikes; +35% for sustained 10-min windows.
- EU: median = 30 GPUs (GDPR isolation enforced in run), 90p = 42. Recommend a separate EU-only reserve to avoid KV sharing risk.
- APAC: median = 18 GPUs, 90p = 26. Latency sensitive window concentrated 02:00-06:00 UTC.

Suggested commit triggers: 
- Auto-commit +20% sustained over 30m triggers a canary tranche for 14 days.
- If 90p predicted load sustained for 2 full days, escalate to full tranche order.

Ops note: these numbers assume we deploy xl-lowmem quantized variant in APAC for cost reasons; if Helix insists on xl-general everywhere add ~25% GPUs across the board.

Attachments: tranche_sim_v1.csv, tranche_map_apac_eu_us.png

Priyom
Priyom Das
Capacity Modeling Lead
Redwood Inference

Please confirm: (1) target model variant (xl-general or xl-lowmem) for initial wave, (2) desired billing cadence for tranche (monthly reserved vs quarterly true-up), (3) acceptance of suggested commit triggers.

Naomi / team —

Thanks for the detailed sims and the SOW. Quick answers: 
1) For the initial wave we want xl-lowmem in APAC and xl-general in US/EU. Can you confirm the +25% delta for xl-general?
2) We prefer quarterly true-up billing for the first 6 months and then evaluate reserved monthly billing afterwards.
3) EU isolation is required — we cannot permit cross-region KV sharing.

One ask: can you provide the estimated additional network egress and compliance cost line items for EU isolation so we can include in our procurement packet?

If you can confirm the numbers, we'll queue legal to review the SOW this week.

—Samira
